subject: POC: Watchtower observability success plan & dashboard sprint
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Tan <sam.tan@watchtower.ai>, Priya Singh <priya@watchtower.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 15:06:00 -0800
Subject: Recap: discovery + proposed observability success criteria and next steps

Hi Sam / Priya —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and the observability-focused success criteria we discussed so we can align on a tight POC: 

1) Goals (what Watchtower needs to validate)
- End-to-end latency breakdown (ingest -> model inference -> postprocess) under expected load (100 rps peak).
- Token-level cost and latency distribution for the top-3 prompt templates.
- Error surface: <0.1% 5xxs and clear root-cause traces for anomalies.
- Full traceability for request IDs across frontend, proxy, and inference nodes.

2) Suggested telemetry to capture during POC
- Metrics: request_latency_p50/p90/p99, tokens_per_request, inference_time_ms, kv_cache_hit_rate, model_cpu/gpu_utilization, batching_efficiency
- Logs: structured request/response metadata (request_id, prompt_hash, model_version), error stack, retry events
- Traces: sampling at 100% for slow requests >500ms and 2% for general traffic; spans for frontend -> routing -> infer -> postprocess
- Exports: daily log export to your S3 bucket + OTLP to your datadog/tempo instance (you mentioned Tempo)

3) Success criteria (binary/clear)
- Dashboards: a prebuilt dashboard for the above metrics that you can use to validate latency/cost targets
- Regression gating: automated alert if token cost increases >10% vs baseline workload
- Ownership: Redwood will ship the dashboard json + a short runbook; Watchtower signs off that the dashboards reflect the POC traffic and metrics

4) Proposed timeline / owners
- Week 0 (this week): finalize success criteria & sign-off on SOW (Sam / Priya)
- Week 1: instrumentation + OTLP ingest + export validation (Redwood: Marissa, Rachel; Watchtower: Priya)
- Week 2: run 3-day synthetic workload + dashboard validation (Watchtower ops + Redwood eng)
- Week 3: joint review, findings, recommended config for production (billing/efficiency notes)

Attachments: I attached a starter metrics spreadsheet with the metric definitions and a sample dashboard export. Also included a SOW draft for the trial scope (sow-draft-v1.pdf).

Next steps: Can you please confirm the success criteria items above and share the S3 bucket path + Tempo endpoint we should use for log/trace export? If that looks good I'll kick off a SOW update and schedule the instrumentation kickoff with Marissa.

Cheers,
Sergio
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

---
Attachment(s): watchtower-poc-metrics.xlsx (spreadsheet), sample-dashboard.json (Grafana dashboard export), sow-draft-v1.pdf (PDF)

From: Sam Tan <sam.tan@watchtower.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Priya Singh <priya@watchtower.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 10:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: discovery + proposed observability success criteria and next steps

Thanks, Sergio — helpful summary. Priya and I chatted after the call; a couple clarifications from our side: 

- For the latency SLA we mentioned 100 rps peak, but our realistic production distribution has long tails from large prompts. Can we define the POC workload as: 70% short (<=128 tokens), 25% medium (129-512), 5% long (>512)? That's what we'll generate for the synthetic run.

- Regarding traces: Tempo is our tracing backend. We can provide an ingest endpoint but would prefer OTLP over Jaeger.

- Dashboards: we'd like one cost-focused dashboard (tokens/cost by prompt template) and one reliability dashboard (error rate, 5xx by component, retry counts). If Redwood can provide the initial templates, we'll iterate.

Small ask: can you include a sample of the dashboard panels in the Drive link so our platform team can estimate integration effort?

On SOW: we'll review sow-draft-v1.pdf and aim to get comments back by EOD Monday.

— Sam
Sam Tan | Head of Platform | Watchtower Analytics
sam.tan@watchtower.ai | +1 (212) 555-0229

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Tan <sam.tan@watchtower.ai>, Priya Singh <priya@watchtower.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: discovery + proposed observability success criteria and next steps

Great — thanks for the clarifications Sam. Quick updates and the action list we will execute: 

1) Workload mix: confirmed. We'll drive the synthetic runner with the distribution you provided. Rachel will param the prompt templates and token distributions.

2) Traces/OTLP: we'll send OTLP lines to your Tempo endpoint. Priya — please send the token/endpoint + any auth details (mTLS cert or API key).

3) Dashboards we'll deliver:
- Cost dashboard (tokens, model cost by prompt template, per-minute token burn)
- Reliability dashboard (5xx by service, retry rates, latency percentiles)
- Inference internals (batch size distribution, kv cache hit, GPU utilization)

Deliverables & owners: 
- Instrumentation checklist (Marissa) — will include log fields to add and OTLP/label mapping
- Dashboard JSON exports (Marissa, Vanessa) — we'll drop the Grafana JSON into the Drive link
- Synthetic runner configs & seed prompts (Rachel)
- SOW update and sign-off tracker (Sergio)

Proposed timeline (dates):
- Mon Feb 16: Receive your Tempo + S3 details and SOW comments (Sam / Priya)
- Tue Feb 17: Redwood pushes instrumentation checklist + Grafana JSONs to Drive
- Wed Feb 18 - Fri Feb 20: Instrumentation & initial ingest validation (Marissa / Rachel + Priya)
- Mon Feb 23 - Wed Feb 25: Synthetic run (3-day window) and dashboard validation
- Thu Feb 26: Joint review meeting (30-45m) to review outcomes and recommend configs

Please reply with confirmation and the endpoint details. If that schedule looks tight on your side we can shift the synthetic run a week later.

Thanks — I'll update the HubSpot deal and attach the new SOW once I have your EOD comments.

Sergio
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Watchtower POC — dashboards, ownership & quick notes

Sergio — copied Vanessa for visibility. Short internal note after reading thread and Sam's reply: 

- I'll own the instrumentation checklist (log field names, OTLP labels) and will produce a one-page runbook for the Watchtower ops team. ETA: Feb 17 EOD PST.
- Vanessa will produce the Grafana JSON panels: cost dashboard (6 panels), reliability (5 panels), inference internals (4 panels). She'll drop sample panels in the Drive link by EOD Feb 17.
- Rachel: please parameterize the synthetic runner with the 70/25/5 distribution and push the seed prompts to the repo under /poc/watchtower/seeds. Notify me when done.

Notes on metrics mapping (so panels are usable on first ingest):
- request_latency_p50/p90/p99 -> panel: latency by prompt_template (use request_id tag)
- tokens_per_request & model_cost_per_token -> panel: tokens & estimated cost per minute
- kv_cache_hit_rate -> panel: cache efficiency over time and histogram
- error_count -> panel: 5xx by component, alert if >0.1% over 30m

I'll attach the checklist and a sample dashboard panel to the Drive link once Vanessa uploads.

One-line: Sam asked for OTLP; Priya will provide endpoint + key. Once we have that we can validate trace ingestion in <24h.

Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
